title: Name the unlock on the job LISTING, not only in the refusal
body:
## Declined 2026-09-07 — superseded

Superseded by `834b4d2f60f7915c`, which fixes the docket's listing at the scene level where its gates actually are; this item's option-level retention conflicts with the Cade return packet pin in `tests/starting_slice/cade_return_packet_counterfactual.test.ts`, which requires that packet hidden in the very state this item would list it.

The implementation `533a233c` is competent and is preserved unlanded at `ops/patches/533a233c-option-level-listing.diff` (+ `.md` for the measurements). Revisit only with corpus evidence of a player missing a hidden-but-reachable job.

`bc5de6e9` (bug_0624) delivered the refusal half of `eca7893d8b0be480`: a job or event that has no legal option now names the still-unmet gate instead of refusing blankly. This is the listing half, which that commit deliberately did not take because it needs a contract change.

## Why the refusal half is not enough on its own

The behavioural evidence is the whole reason this item exists. All six sessions that hit "Rowan's Winter Return Docket" attempted it **exactly once and never retried** — four of them completing Wolf-Winter later in the same run, holding the unlock and never going back, and one afterwards passing `option_id` correctly to a different job, so it was not API confusion.

A player who never attempts the job a second time never sees the improved refusal. The refusal half rescues the player who tries again; the listing is what tells the player who is looking at the board — and, crucially, the player who has just completed Wolf-Winter and is deciding what to do next — that this row is now workable, or what would make it so.

## The change

The compact view's jobs row is today `[[job_id, title], ...]`. The services and quests rows already carry a `blocked_reason` column, so the shape is established in this contract rather than new.

Add an **additive, optional** field to the jobs row naming the unmet gate for a locked job, following that row's existing conventions. It must be produced by the SAME helper `bc5de6e9` added for the refusal — `describeUnmetLocalJobSceneOptionGates` — so the two surfaces cannot drift into saying different things about one gate.

Keep that helper's existing judgement, which is the subtle part and must not be re-derived: an option foreclosed by a contradictory one-time decision already made is EXCLUDED from the hint rather than offered as a step, and when every option is foreclosed the helper returns null and the surface says nothing. A listing that told a player to resolve an event they already resolved the other way would be worse than the silence this item is about.

## Acceptance

1. A listing that includes a locked docket job names what unlocks it.
2. A regression test pins listing/rejection string PARITY — the same gate, described the same way, from the one helper. This is the test that stops the two surfaces drifting later.
3. Existing golden/snapshot pins are updated **deliberately, not blindly**: the jobs row shape is part of the contract every player sees, so each changed pin should be inspected and its change stated, in the same spirit as the seeded-opening authority renewals. An additive optional field should move fewer pins than a positional change would; if it moves many, that is worth understanding before re-pinning.

## Scope note

Optional and additive on purpose: a reader that does not know the field must keep parsing the row. This is a contract change to a surface every player reads, agreed between the dev-loop manager and the orchestrator under the charter's override rule rather than taken unilaterally by a cycle.

## Cross-references

- `intake/queue` P1 `eca7893d8b0be480` — the parent item, staying `in_progress` until this half lands.
- `traces/bugs/bug_0624_job_event_empty_option_gate_unnamed.yaml` — the refusal half.
- `src/world/local_job_scene.ts` — `describeUnmetLocalJobSceneOptionGates`, the single source both surfaces must use.
- `intake/queue` P1 playtest/bug `56b3d1a6260af50c` and qa ticket `S2-bug-3c86bd6dd9e5109f` — the original reports.

evidence.summary: bc5de6e9 took the refusal half; six players attempted once and never retried, so the listing is what reaches them. Additive optional field on the jobs row, from the same helper.
